posts.cooked:
Ok so I played SotM for the first time last week and I had a blast.  We had a full team of five against Citizen Dawn in the Ruins of Atlantis and I was playing Visionary.  Now, some of the first cards I pulled were Prophetic Vision and Suggestion and I thought they'd be very useful in "warning" my team of what was coming up, but the other players told me that I could look and manipulate the deck, but that I could not discuss what I saw with them.

I skimmed through the rulebook and couldn't find that rule anywhere, but I went a long with it and kept my mouth shut about what was coming up.

Is it true that when you have abilities that let you look in a deck you cannot speak about what you find with your team?

We play the same as your group wanted to.  Reveals are to the player that played the card, and if they wish to share info they can, but you don't show the cards.

There is no oficial ruling either way, so I'd say if your group doesn't want to show the cards, don't.

I don't know why we do it that way, I do find it more fun, and there is never any arguing over what card went where.

 

We also play with our hands visible, but mostly because it saves time discussing what everyone can do.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
I don't see the point in playing a reveal-cards-and-decide type card unless you're going to use that info to help the group. Part of the fun is in planning what you can do together. We often have little discussions about which card to put on top and which on the bottom, taking into consideration what everyone's planning to do this turn and what cards they have. There seems to be an unwritten consensus that the person who played the card gets the final decision but the other players definitely have input. 

Think about it in terms of a solo game where you're playing three heroes. If you know a particular card's coming up you'll respond to that with every hero you control, because it's impossible to un-know that information. A three-player, three-hero game should be no different.

I have no problem with sharing all the inormation.  Just stating that there isn't an official ruling on whether revealed cards are shown to everyone or just the person that is using the effect.  We don't show, but we tend to play in ways that keep the game moving, as our discussion tends to get long winded and drag games out.  One of the reasons I like playing Visionary is because you get to manipulate the game and other people.

I like knowing that with a TtE on another heroes character I can change their damage to anything I want, with or without their permission.

(That has only happened once) and that I can put whatever cards I want wherever I want, It really fits the characters "MY MIND IS MORE POWERFUL THAN YOUR TEAM!" shtick.

You can play cooperativel without playing nice, or doing what the group wants.  Just play how your group likes to play.
